text: How an industrial arm is built: joints, degrees of freedom, the work envelope, coordinate frames, the tool center point, and how a controller interpolates joint and straight-line moves.
How industrial robots are programmed: online or offline, in environments like RobotStudio and PolyScope, in vendor languages, and with vendor-agnostic ROS.
Why ROS exists: a common, vendor-agnostic layer for programming robots from different makers.
How to choose and size grippers, mount them and set payload, and program the digital I/O that opens a gripper, confirms a grip and talks to a PLC, in URScript and RAPID.
How robot programs are organized (RAPID modules and routines, URScript functions and threads) and how they recover from errors such as a missed pick, with a 3 by 3 palletizing loop.

How robots use cameras to pick parts that are not in a fixed place: 2D versus 3D guidance, camera mounting, lens and hand-eye calibration, and the frame-shift math that turns a vision result into a correct pick.
What open source is, how to make a first contribution, how robotics projects like ROS 2 and MoveIt work, and a lab where you open a real pull request.
Build a ROS 2 Lyrical Python package from scratch: workspaces and overlays, ros2 pkg create, setup.py and package.xml, rosdep, colcon, and a timer-driven node that drives Turtlesim in a square.
Plan and execute arm motions with MoveIt 2 on ROS 2 Lyrical: URDF and SRDF, ros2_control mock hardware, move_group, OMPL and Pilz PTP/LIN, and a UR5e in RViz.

Where AI is really used in industrial robotics as of October 2026 (learned vision, predictive maintenance, LLM coding assistants, research foundation models), what the evidence says about AI-written code, and how to check it before it moves a real arm.

How robots turn a target into smooth setpoints: trapezoidal, triangular and S-curve profiles, cubic and quintic time scaling, joint, linear and circular interpolation, zones, and time parameterization in MoveIt.
The full math of a planar two-link arm: forward kinematics, the reachable ring, closed-form inverse kinematics with atan2, rounding edge cases, and the Jacobian singularity.
Industrial camera sensors and optics: CMOS versus CCD, global and rolling shutters, pixel size and Nyquist resolution, focal length and f-number, telecentric lenses, and GenICam.
Core 2D image processing: color space conversion, histograms and contrast equalization, global, Otsu and adaptive thresholding, contours, moments, blobs, Canny edge detection, and template matching.

3D perception for robotics: direct sensing versus 2D inference, stereo disparity geometry, point cloud filtering with PCL (PassThrough, VoxelGrid, outliers), RANSAC planes, Euclidean clustering, and bin picking.

Build a ROS 2 camera pipeline in Python: sensor_msgs/Image and CameraInfo, optical frames, image_transport, cv_bridge conversion, and real-time OpenCV edge processing; runs without a camera using cam2image test images.
From discrete wiring to industrial networks: sinking and sourcing (NPN/PNP), fieldbus history, line, star and ring topologies, cyclic versus acyclic data, and Device Level Ring recovery.
Lab: the UR Modbus TCP server and its general-purpose registers, packing handshake bits in URScript, and writing and reading registers from Python with pymodbus (stand-in server, no hardware).
How a mobile robot finds its position, sees obstacles, plans and follows a path, and recovers when it gets stuck, following the open-source Nav2 project.
Four projects with milestones and rubrics: a simulated work cell, a ROS 2 pick-and-place with MoveIt 2, a speed-controlled wheel, and an open-source cell monitor.
Capstone project: build a pick-and-place task for a simulated UR5e with ROS 2, MoveIt 2 and the MoveIt Task Constructor on mock hardware or Gazebo, with milestones, tests and a rubric.

Capstone project: an open-source ROS 2 cell monitor that reads robot state, packed Modbus handshake bits and a camera check from stand-in servers, keeps a maintenance log, and ends with a real pull request. No hardware needed.
